summary: Omega-6 fatty acids are a polyunsaturated-fat family that includes linoleic acid and arachidonic acid. Linoleic acid must be obtained from the diet.

functions.description: Omega-6 fatty acids are a polyunsaturated-fat family that includes linoleic acid and arachidonic acid. Linoleic acid must be obtained from the diet.

foodSourceRules.notes: Qualitative source education only. Missing measurements and fatty-acid totals are not reconstructed from other concepts.

deficiency.overview: The source establishes that linoleic acid is essential; an unavailable total omega-6 food value or a short food log does not diagnose essential-fatty-acid deficiency.
deficiency.medicalBoundary: Symptoms are nonspecific and cannot diagnose a nutrient deficiency. Diagnosis may require clinical evaluation and appropriate laboratory testing.

excess.overview: No universal omega-6-to-omega-3 ratio or personal omega-6 ceiling is derived from this source.
excess.medicalBoundary: No upper limit is an intake goal. Individual clinical or medical assessment requires a qualified professional.

claims.text: Omega-6 fatty acids are a polyunsaturated-fat family that includes linoleic acid and arachidonic acid. Linoleic acid must be obtained from the diet.
